title: All 44 Surviving Oriire School Hostages Rescued in Multi-Agency Operation
detail: In the evening of Friday, July 10 — 56 days after the May 15 mass abduction — a combined force of the Nigerian Army, Navy Special Forces, Special Boat Service, Air Force special forces, Police special force, and the Department of State Services executed an intelligence-led rescue operation that freed the remaining 44 hostages (37 pupils and 7 teachers) taken from three schools in Oriire LGA, Oyo State. The Army described the release as 'unconditional,' with no ransom or prisoner exchange conceded to the kidnappers despite their earlier demand for the release of a detained gang leader, who remains in custody facing prosecution. Eight members of the kidnapping gang were arrested and handed to the DSS. Of the original 46 abducted, one teacher was killed on the spot during the raid and a second, Michael Oyedokun, was killed in captivity, leaving 44 to be rescued. The resolution ends a crisis that triggered a month-long Nigeria Union of Teachers strike and protests across Oyo and Osun states.

sources.name: Federal Ministry of Information and National Orientation

title: Fubara Presents 2026 Budget to Rivers Assembly Amid Signs of Political Thaw
detail: Governor Siminalayi Fubara formally presented the 2026 Appropriation Bill to the Rivers State House of Assembly on July 10 at the House of Assembly Quarters Auditorium in Port Harcourt, in a session broadcast live and marked by a visibly tense atmosphere. Following the presentation, Speaker Martins Amaewhule — an ally of FCT Minister Nyesom Wike — held a brief conversation with Fubara and the two shook hands, a gesture read as a sign of easing tension in the protracted Fubara-Wike political standoff. The peace remains fragile: the earlier reconciliation accord, under which Fubara agreed not to seek re-election in 2027 and to join the APC, had appeared to be collapsing in May and June as both camps jockeyed for position ahead of the 2027 governorship race.
